Those are two things I've been harping on Texans receivers needing to improve over the last couple of years.

Also some really encouraging effort and execution as a blocker, both in the run game and on passing plays, including Jaylin Noel's explosive catch and run.

For a guy who was just traded, had to learn a new offense and traveled across three time zones in the same week, there's a lot to be encouraged about from these 12 snaps.

Washington is averaging 3.2 targets a game, so this needs a specific matchup case. TB gives us one.

TB plays single high on 64.8% of charted snaps. Washington’s TPRR jumps from 5.9% against two high to 20.3% against single high. He’s caught 8 of 12 targets for 110 Yds against those looks.

Now look at what TB allows to TEs in single high: 14 catches on 17 targets, 169 Yds and 2 TDs. That’s 82.4% completions and 9.9 Yds per target.

Washington aligns inline on 75% of his snaps. PIT can show run, make the underneath defenders respect it, then release him into a route. TB allowing just 3.37 Yds per carry to RBs adds some appeal to throwing from those formations near the goal line.

He already has 3 end zone targets and 15% of PIT’s red zone targets. There’s also a second way home: 8.3 YAC per catch and +0.60 YAC over expectation. 

His TD against CLE came from 21 Yds out. He doesn’t need every scoring chance delivered from the 1.

PIT being without Roman Wilson, Skowronek and Pittman helps the opportunity case. Keep an eye on TB’s injury report too: Winfield missed Wednesday practice and Dennis was limited. Their availability matters through the middle also.

That’s why ATD is my main bet. The 2+ is a tiny add on: one short TD off a heavy look, then another red zone chance or a catch he turns into something bigger. We can only hope.
